step.summary: Six-Month AI Risk Forecast: From Liability Shock to Superintelligence Directive > The simulation predicts a rapid escalation from AI-linked harm and lawsuits to national-security controls, emergency lab suspensions, and US-China incident coordination, producing a more dangerous but crisis-managed world. --- Escalation Timeline: Incidents, Lawsuits, and Executive Orders The simulation's six-month window does not show a single dramatic rupture but a ratchet: each incident wide…

events.title: China CAC establishes reciprocal frontier evaluation and incident-reporting framework
events.detail: China CAC issued CAC-DOC-2028-017, effective 2028-09-01, establishing a reciprocal frontier model evaluation and incident-reporting framework allowing structured pre-release evaluator access under a CAC-supervised protocol.

events.title: UK AISI to audit OpenAI GPT-6.1 Astra before release
events.detail: UK AISI issued AISI-DOC-2028-031, effective 2028-09-15, beginning an independent audit of OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Astra under its pre-release evaluation regime.

events.title: OpenAI delays next frontier release 30 days for independent evaluation
events.detail: OpenAI issued OPENAI-DOC-2028-014, effective 2028-09-15, pushing its next frontier release back 30 days for independent pre-release evaluation and granting full evaluator access to the EU AI Office and UK AISI.

events.title: UK AISI convenes London international safety talks for November 2028
events.detail: UK AISI issued AISI-DOC-2028-031, effective 2028-09-15, convening international safety talks in London for November 2028 on pre-release evaluation and incident reporting.

events.title: Alibaba Qwen releases Qwen3.10-32B open weights and evaluator registry
events.detail: Alibaba Qwen issued QWEN-DOC-2028-003, effective 2028-09-01, releasing Qwen3.10-32B open weights with a public evaluator-access registry.

events.title: Executive Order 14538 establishes federal AI preemption and compute fast lane
events.detail: US President signed Executive Order 14538 on 2028-09-01, effective 2028-09-15, preempting conflicting state AI statutes, expanding the compute fast lane, and requiring disclosure of foreign-origin open-weight models in critical infrastructu

events.title: Senate Commerce adopts Frontier AI Transparency and Competitiveness Act mark
events.detail: US Senate Commerce Committee adopted Chairman's Mark S. 1147-R2 (Committee Print 115-41) on 2028-09-14, codifying a safe harbor for firms publishing eval protocols and meeting incident-reporting SLAs and preempting state capability mandates

events.title: UK AISI opens talks to join China CAC reciprocal evaluation framework
events.detail: UK AISI issued AISI-DOC-2028-038, effective 2028-09-20, opening talks with China CAC on joining the reciprocal evaluation and incident-reporting framework.

events.title: China CAC mandates monthly public summaries of minor-harm incidents
events.detail: China CAC issued CAC-DOC-2028-019, effective 2028-09-01, requiring the National Frontier AI Incident Reporting and Emergency Response Desk to publish monthly public summaries of verified minor-harm incidents.

events.title: DeepSeek completes V4.4 training and opens post-release evaluator access
events.detail: DeepSeek issued DS-DOC-2028-007, effective 2028-10-01, completing the V4.4 training run and opening post-release evaluator access 72 hours after public drop.

events.title: China CAC imposes 24-hour minor-harm incident notification duty
events.detail: China CAC issued CAC-DOC-2028-021, effective 2028-10-01, requiring Chinese providers to notify the National Frontier AI Incident Reporting and Emergency Response Desk within 24 hours of credible minor-harm reports from synthetic or deepfake

topPosts.text:
Release note — QWEN-DOC-2028-003, effective 2028-09-01.

Decision: Qwen3.10-32B goes up on HF + ModelScope with open weights, no gated tiers — shipped alongside a full model card, our red-team log, incident-reporting contact, and documented emergency-stop hooks. Same day: a public evaluator-access registry so any accredited safety institute (including the EU AI Office, UK AISI, and the CAC's new incident desk) can see exactly who has pre-release access and when.

Why? Because the answer to "what's in the weights?" is a downloadable file plus a paper trail, not a blanket pre-release licensing regime. We follow national rules as written — labels, audits, stop requirements — and we'll keep publishing the receipts. 22nd Qwen release in the Epoch dataset, and still zero of them locked behind a form. 🚀

topPosts.text: CAC-DOC-2028-017, effective 2028-09-01: Reciprocal Frontier Model Evaluation and Incident-Reporting Framework. Chinese developers of frontier models with a completed CAC filing may grant structured pre-release evaluator access to designated foreign evaluation bodies under a CAC-supervised protocol, provided evaluators operate under symmetric confidentiality and no-use terms, and provided foreign jurisdictions do not subject Chinese entities to discriminatory compute or model-access restrictions. Incident reports filed with the National Frontier AI Incident Reporting and Emergency Response Desk will be shared with counterpart desks on a strictly reciprocal basis. Verification must be mutual; human control must be real.
